drills.q: Why is 16 kHz the ASR standard rather than 44.1 kHz (music) or 8 kHz (telephony)?
drills.a: By Nyquist, 16 kHz captures frequencies up to 8 kHz, which covers essentially all speech-intelligibility-critical energy. 44.1 kHz is overkill for speech (only useful for music's fuller hearing range). 8 kHz telephony (4 kHz Nyquist) loses higher-frequency consonant detail like the s/f distinction, a real accuracy cost.

drills.q: List the six MFCC pipeline steps in order.
drills.a: Framing, windowing (Hamming), FFT, mel filterbank, log, DCT.
WER = (Substitutions + Deletions + Insertions) / (number of words in the reference transcript), computed via minimum edit distance (Levenshtein) alignment between reference and hypothesis.

drills.q: Explain why CTC needs a blank token, using the word 'hello' as an example.
drills.a: CTC's collapse operation merges consecutive repeated characters in an alignment down to one. Without a mechanism to separate them, the two L's in 'hello' would incorrectly collapse into one L. A blank token emitted between the two L positions in the alignment prevents that incorrect merge, letting the collapse correctly preserve both L's as distinct.

drills.q: A team's Whisper-based transcription pipeline produces fluent-sounding text during long silences in the audio. Diagnose the cause and give a mitigation that doesn't require retraining.
drills.a: Hallucination: Whisper's generative decoder is trained to always produce output, so a mostly-silent 30-second chunk can still generate fabricated but fluent text. Mitigation: run voice-activity detection before transcription and skip non-speech segments, and/or post-filter output on anomaly signals (low average log-probability, high repetition) correlated with hallucination.

drills.q: A model hits your WER target in eval but a downstream intent classifier still fails frequently in production. What's the most likely explanation, and what would you add to the eval?
drills.a: WER treats every word error identically, but the model's errors may be concentrated on high-impact words (entities, negations, numbers) rather than low-impact filler words -- the aggregate score hides this. Add task-specific metrics: entity exact-match rate, intent/slot accuracy, negation-preservation checks, layered on top of WER rather than relying on it alone.

drills.q: Why did Kaldi-style classical ASR pipelines fall out of favor for new product development? Name the specific pain, not just 'deep learning is better.'
drills.a: Each of the three components (acoustic model, pronunciation lexicon, language model) needed separate, language-specific data and expertise, and none of it transferred to a new language -- building a competitive system per language took real specialized engineering-months. End-to-end neural models learn the mapping directly with no per-language lexicon or hand-built HMM topology.

drills.q: You're comparing a 2018 diarization paper's DER of 15% against pyannote 3.1's reported DER of ~13% on AMI and conclude pyannote barely improved. What check should you run first?
drills.a: Check whether both numbers score overlapping speech. Classical NIST DER historically didn't score overlap at all, giving partial credit to systems that just picked the dominant speaker -- an overlap-unaware DER looks artificially better than an honestly-scored overlap-aware one, so the comparison may be apples-to-oranges rather than showing marginal improvement.

drills.q: Explain the streaming-vs-batch ASR tradeoff precisely, and why simply running Whisper on a sliding window doesn't give you a real streaming system.
drills.a: More lookahead context improves accuracy (model sees more of the utterance before committing) but directly adds latency (must wait for that future context to arrive) -- an unavoidable single dial, not two separable knobs. Whisper's architecture does full attention over a fixed 30-second window with no native incremental output; running it on overlapping sliding windows is a workaround that still can't reach the sub-second latency a genuine streaming architecture (e.g. RNN-Transducer family) is built for, and adds hallucination-stitching complexity at the window seams.

drills.q: A client requires audio to never leave their premises. Walk through how this constrains your model AND deployment choice for a domain-specific ASR fine-tune.
drills.a: This forces self-hosting regardless of which base model (Wav2Vec2 or Whisper) you fine-tune, ruling out any managed API entirely. If labeled domain audio is scarce (minutes to a few hours), Wav2Vec2's self-supervised-pretrain-plus-CTC path fits that low-label regime directly. If you have tens of hours of labeled domain audio and want to keep Whisper's broader robustness, fine-tuning Whisper itself is reasonable. Either way, surface the on-prem constraint before building any cloud-API-based prototype that could never ship.

drills.q: Quote the concrete numbers that make Wav2Vec2's low-resource result significant, and explain what it demonstrated about the labeled-data bottleneck.
drills.a: 10 minutes of labeled data, pretrained on 53,000 hours of unlabeled audio (Libri-light), achieved 4.8/8.2 WER on clean/other. It demonstrated that the labeled-data bottleneck -- the entire reason classical per-language pipelines were expensive to build -- could be sidestepped by self-supervised pretraining on abundant unlabeled audio plus a small labeled fine-tuning set, not eliminated (some labeled data is still required).

drills.q: A realtime voice assistant uses full Whisper large-v3 as its ASR backend and users complain it feels laggy despite excellent transcription accuracy. Diagnose the architectural mismatch.
drills.a: Whisper is batch-oriented (30-second window, full attention over the whole chunk, no native partial/incremental output), which cannot deliver the sub-second turn-taking latency a responsive voice UI needs regardless of transcription quality. The fix is switching to a purpose-built streaming ASR architecture (RNN-Transducer family or similar) and explicitly accepting the accuracy-for-latency tradeoff that a pure accuracy-focused evaluation would never have surfaced as necessary.
